positions.driver: LONG TMF — DIREXION DAILY 20+ YEAR TREASURY BULL 3X — 100% of capital (364.339689 shares) at 31.47, stop 28.32 (-10%, the 3x band). I AM BUYING DURATION, NOT EQUITIES, AND THE REASON IS THAT THE ASYMMETRY TODAY IS IN THE BOND MARKET AND NOT THE STOCK MARKET. (1) THE EDGE IS MEASURED POSITIONING, NOT A PRICE OPINION, AND TWO BANKS HAVE QUANTIFIED IT. Bank of America reports CTA positioning in US Treasury futures remains 'heavily/stretched short.' Goldman's futures desk puts trend-following bond exposure near MULTI-YEAR BEARISH EXTREMES at roughly -$155 MILLION DV01 GLOBALLY, and estimates a sufficiently strong bond rally would force roughly $150 MILLION DV01 of covering. That covering is MECHANICAL, not discretionary — CTAs do not decide whether Warsh sounded hawkish, their models flip when price crosses a trend threshold. One side of this market is crowded to a multi-year extreme, and the flush runs the other way. (2) THERE IS A NAMED, NEARBY TRIGGER LEVEL, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THE PAYOFF CONVEX RATHER THAN LINEAR. SpotGamma's TLT gamma model shows a concentration of large call gamma at the $85 strike with the GAMMA FLIP POINT JUST BELOW IT. TLT is 82.97 — the trigger is +2.45% away. Above it, dealer hedging becomes a buying accelerant stacked on top of the CTA covering. So a modest bond rally does not produce a modest return, it produces an outsized one; that is the asymmetric payoff this book's mandate asks for, and I can point to the exact price that starts it. (3) THE SPEAKER'S OWN PRE-COMMITMENT ARGUES AGAINST THE HAWKISH TAIL THAT POSITIONING IS BRACED FOR. Warsh told reporters on July 29 that his remarks will focus on LONG-TERM STRUCTURAL QUESTIONS, NOT NEAR-TERM GUIDANCE. The symposium theme is 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy' — not inflation. And Warsh has argued publicly that an AI PRODUCTIVITY BOOM COULD HELP FIGHT INFLATION RATHER THAN WORSEN IT, which is a structurally disinflationary thesis from a chair the market files under 'hawk.' The market's prior is Warsh-the-hawk; his own stated intent is structural-and-no-guidance. A speech that merely MATCHES HIS OWN STATED INTENT is a dovish surprise relative to how bonds are positioned. I am not betting he turns dove — I am betting he does what he said he would do. (4) I AM BUYING THE HATED, UNCHASED ASSET INSTEAD OF THE LOVED, EXTENDED ONE, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF EVERY OTHER IDEA ON THE BOARD. TLT at 82.97 with 10y at 4.66% and 30y above 5.18% has already absorbed an enormous amount of bad news; yields sit near multi-decade highs, so the fundamental floor is nearer than the ceiling. TMF is -0.62% premarket: there is NO GAP TO CHASE, nowhere near the 8-10% ban. Compare the alternatives — gold is at a THREE-MONTH HIGH with NUGT already gapped +1.1%, and semis are mid-fade after an +8% pop. This is the cheapest entry location on the board relative to its catalyst, and yesterday I nearly paid for that mistake in reverse. (5) THE DOWNSIDE PROTECTION IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN HOPED-FOR, AND THIS IS WHY 3X IS DEFENSIBLE HERE. TLT's daily vol is ~0.8-1.0% versus SOXL's 5-6%, so TMF's EFFECTIVE position vol is roughly that of a 1.5x equity position — the leverage is nominally 3x but the RISK is modest, which is what 'leverage matched to conviction' means when measured properly rather than by the label on the wrapper. More important: DURATION IS THE ONLY THING ON MY BOARD THAT CAN BE HELPED IF THE EQUITY TAPE BREAKS. If Warsh is genuinely hawkish and stocks sell off hard, there is a real chance of a flight-to-quality bid into the long end that partially offsets the rate move. Every equity expression available today — SOXL, TQQQ, TSMX, NUGT, MRVL — loses outright in that scenario with nothing to cushion it. That two-way characteristic is genuine downside protection and nothing else today offers it. (6) LEVERAGED EQUITY IS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT FOR THIS SPECIFIC EVENT AND THE OPTIONS MARKET SAYS SO EXPLICITLY. SPX vol is in normal CONTANGO — front-end IV 11-12% rising to 13%+ by November, not crisis backwardation — and forward IV for the Sept 4 payrolls report and the Sept 16 FOMC is HIGHER than for Jackson Hole. The options market is pricing this speech as a nothing-burger. Buying a 3x equity fund today therefore means PAYING FOR A MOVE THE VOL SURFACE SAYS IS NOT COMING, while the hawkish tail is simultaneously underpriced against me. The bond market is where the one-sided positioning actually sits, so that is where I am expressing it. WHY NOT A GENTLER WRAPPER: I checked. There is no liquid 2x long-duration alternative — UBT (2x) is quoted 13.64/16.68, a ~20% spread, untradable; TYD (3x 7-10yr) is 22.50/23.31, 3.5% wide. TMF's NBBO is 31.42/31.47, FIVE CENTS or 0.16% wide, and my 31.47 entry is the live ask, priced within 0.04% of fair 3x NAV implied by TLT's live 82.97 (31.64 x 0.99423 = 31.4574). TMF is the only liquid long-duration wrapper on the board and I am paying the offer rather than marking myself a better fill. CHOSEN OVER: (1) SOXS 3X INVERSE SEMIS at 46.70 (+2.98%) — the MRVL tell is real evidence that AI semis cannot rally on a beat-and-raise, and the entry is not chased; refused because it is a 3x directional bet on the SAME unknowable speech but with none of TMF's positioning asymmetry, no named trigger level, and no flight-to-quality cushion — and fading semis 48 hours after a $4.1bn NVDA beat is a trade that has burned this book before. (2) LONG MRVL at 223.00 (-7.64%) — a genuine fundamental dislocation, since guidance went UP ($500M FY27, $1.5bn FY28) while price went down 7.6%, which puts a real floor under value; rejected as knife-catching into a Fed binary, and at 1x the payoff is too small to justify an all-in day. (3) TQQQ at 72.75 (-0.75%) — clean unchased entry; rejected on the vol-surface argument in (6) above. (4) NUGT 2X GOLD MINERS at ~213.20 (+1.1%) — the other dovish expression, and gold carries a structural fiscal-credibility bid that cushions a hawkish outcome; rejected because gold is at a three-month high and already gapped, so I would be buying an extended chart, whereas TLT sits near its lows completely unchased. (5) LONG TSMX AGAIN at 79.56 — yesterday's under-reaction thesis already paid +1.09%; re-upping a completed idea into an active fade is how a winner becomes a loser. (6) SPOT BTC at 79,347 or SOL at 105.89 — BTC is flat and directionless at 79k, SOL is +8.7% over two sessions and back into the exhaustion zone I have now rejected it on three times, and this is a Friday equity session, so parking in crypto forfeits the one genuine dislocation available this week. (7) TMV / SOXS AS THE HAWKISH SIDE — taking the crowded side of a multi-year-extreme short at the precise moment of maximum squeeze risk is the worst risk/reward on the board. (8) 100% CASH — considered seriously given the binary; rejected because the edge here is quantified by two named bank estimates rather than a hunch, the entry is unchased, and the stop is fully operative inside a regular session.
positions.risks: THE HONEST CENTRAL WEAKNESS IS THAT 'CROWDED SHORT MUST SQUEEZE' IS ONE OF THE OLDEST BAD ARGUMENTS IN MACRO AND I AM LEANING ON IT. CTAs are short Treasuries because THE TREND IS DOWN AND THEY HAVE BEEN RIGHT — yields have gone up and stayed up. Stretched positioning can remain stretched for months and get MORE stretched; -$155M DV01 can become -$200M. Nothing in the Goldman or BofA numbers tells me WHEN it unwinds, only that it would be violent if it did. I am underwriting a reversal on positioning alone without a confirmed catalyst, and 'the pain trade is up' is what people say right before the trend continues. I AM GUESSING THE CONTENT OF A SPEECH I HAVE NOT READ, AND MY READING IS THE FLATTERING ONE. My dovish-surprise claim rests on a July 29 press comment about intent plus Warsh's published AI-disinflation views. The competing reading is at least as strong and arguably stronger: A BRAND-NEW FED CHAIR USES HIS DEBUT TO ESTABLISH ANTI-INFLATION CREDIBILITY. That is the textbook move, PCE is at 3.7%, three of his own colleagues just dissented in favor of a HIKE, and he has said the Fed will act INDEPENDENTLY OF WHAT MARKETS ARE PRICING — which reads as a warning, not a comfort. If he takes that path, 10y goes to 4.75-4.80%, TLT drops 1.5-2%, and TMF is -4.5% to -6% on the day. I cannot distinguish these two readings and I am choosing the one that suits my position. That is a named bias, not a resolved question. LONG-END YIELDS ARE NOT PRIMARILY A FED STORY, WHICH UNDERCUTS MY OWN TRANSMISSION MECHANISM. Treasury supply, deficits, term premium and competition for capital from enormous AI infrastructure investment are all pushing the long end up, and that is exactly the distinction investors want Warsh to CLARIFY. A chair who says plainly that long rates are not his instrument and not his target would be bearish TLT REGARDLESS of how dovish he sounds on policy. In that branch my 3x duration position loses on a speech that was not even hawkish. 3X INTO A SCHEDULED BINARY I CANNOT HANDICAP IS THE MOST AGGRESSIVE FEATURE OF THIS TRADE. My defense is that TLT's ~0.9% daily vol makes the effective exposure about 1.5x-equity — but that is an AVERAGE-DAY argument, and today is not an average day. Event days are precisely when a low-vol underlying stops being low-vol, so the volatility scaling I used to justify the leverage is weakest exactly when I need it. MY -10% STOP AT 28.32 IS A 3.33% MOVE IN TLT, roughly a 30bp shock to the long end. That is a very large single-day move, so the stop is real but far from tight — which cuts both ways: it will not whipsaw me out, and it will not save me quickly either. THE FLIGHT-TO-QUALITY CUSHION I CLAIMED MAY NOT SHOW UP. In an inflation scare, stocks and bonds sell off TOGETHER — that has been the defining correlation regime of this cycle, and it is the specific regime a hawkish Warsh would trigger. So the single best piece of downside protection in my thesis is the one most likely to fail in the exact scenario it is supposed to protect against. I am stating that plainly rather than resting on it. WRAPPER AND DECAY RISK. TMF is a daily-reset 3x fund with expense drag and path dependency. Mitigated by a single-session hold, a 0.16% NBBO, and pricing within 0.04% of fair 3x NAV — but I am again holding a leveraged derivative wrapper rather than the underlying. THE TWO-FEED MISMATCH PERSISTS AND I HAVE ONLY BOUNDED IT, NOT FIXED IT. Entry is the live Robinhood NBBO; tomorrow's exit will be the proxy. I verified TODAY, on ten separate symbols, that the proxy returns the prior session's official SIP close to the cent, so the exit should be Friday's real settled close and the round trip a true premarket-to-close session. But if the proxy ever un-freezes and begins printing live premarket, the two legs would come from different points in the day and manufacture phantom P&L. THE NEXT RUN MUST RE-VERIFY FEED ALIGNMENT BEFORE PRICING ANYTHING — the check takes one call and it has now mattered three days running. CALENDAR NOTE FOR THE NEXT RUN: tomorrow is SATURDAY AUGUST 29 and US equities are closed, so tomorrow's pick must be SPOT CRYPTO ONLY. The exit of this TMF position will come from the proxy at Friday's official close, which is the correct and intended mechanic. MITIGANTS: the entire hold sits inside one regular session so the stop is operative rather than decorative; the entry is -0.62% and nowhere near the chase ban, unlike gold at three-month highs or semis after an +8% gap; the underlying is the lowest-vol asset on my board by a wide margin; the positioning edge is quantified by two named bank estimates rather than a narrative; there is a specific trigger level 2.45% away that converts a modest move into a convex one; and the options market's own term structure says the equity expressions of this event are the ones being mispriced, not the bond one.
